beginner_version.found: Tiny separate things: none (no houses, people, posts). Textures of hundreds of items: no; busy measured 0.7% fine texture, three tiles on the wing-tail edge and one foot, which are the bird's own detail, not a field of items. Detail inside big shapes one mark can't make: no; the background is soft blurred foliage masses and trunks, the bark is one repeated short stroke. Parts: about 8 (background glow, sun, far trunks, far foliage, the trunk and branch, the leaves, the bird), within max_parts 8 at this size.
beginner_version.why: Every answer is no, so the lesson is made from the fitted photo, with no beginner render.

canvas_fit.canvas: 16 x 12 in, landscape (default: the standard size closest to the photo's 3:2 shape)
canvas_fit.lost: about 0.9 in worth (5.6%) of hazy forest off each side, about 11% in all; the far left trunk edge and the right-hand twig tips get a little shorter
canvas_fit.why: No --canvas was given; fit-canvas picked 12x16 landscape, and a crop keeps the whole bird, its feet, the branch and the sun.

photo_prep.subject: a black-capped chickadee perched on a curved brown branch, four autumn leaves, a hazy blue-and-orange autumn forest behind with a soft sun at upper right
photo_prep.why: An AI-made painting with no bars, borders, captions or frame around it; everything in the image is the scene.
